# Acknowledgements

This thesis, and the work contained within, would not have been possible without the wonderful support of an incredibly talented group of scholars and experts in their fields. I survived the process! All thanks to:


- **My supervisor, Dr. Maria Byrne**. I am both honoured and grateful to be your student and collaborator. You are the most dedicated mentor that I have ever met. Thank you for all the opportunities that you have facilitated throughout these years. I am proud to have you as my supervisor, I also hope that I have, at the very least, met your expectations as a PhD student.
- **Dr. Sebastian Holmes**. Thanks, Seb, for believing in my work and encouraging me to push on. I am grateful for all the opportunities to work with you. Your commitment to get me through my final undergraduate year was the reason that I have not given up on academia!
- **Dr. Hong Dao Nguyen**. Without a doubt the most cheerful person I have ever met. Thanks for helping me get through the first year! And for being there for both friendship and advice. 
- **Dr. Christina McGraw**.  You made a programmer out of me, and I am still amazed that I can do so much with just a syringe pump, a spectrometer, and bunch of tubes. Thank you for your patience and kindness!
- **Dr. Jon Havenhand**. You probably don't know it, but your introduction to R was one of the main reasons why I started using the programming language, and your encouraging words on my Excel template on analysing respirometry led to the decision to develop the R package that is now a chapter in this book. Thank you!
- **Dr. Nicholas Carey**. You made a better physiologist out of me, and chatting with you is always great fun. Thanks for the great advice on respirometry and the great collaboration on the R package! I can call myself a physiologist because of you.
- **Dr. Steven Doo**. One day, Steve decided to force himself to learn R by re-analysing all his data using the programming language. \textit{What a great idea}, I thought! So I tried to do the same... and wrote this entire thesis in R. Didn't expect that, but thanks Steve.
- **Sergio Torres-Gabarda**. I couldn't have asked for a better lab mate and friend. You've really made the PhD experience that much easier by being there, sometimes magically, every time when I needed it. It's like having extra hands, because you're that good at reading my mind sometimes...did that mean I had 4 hands?
- **Joshua Aldridge**. Josh is probably the real reason why I was able to set up my experiments. He taught me everything I needed to know on how to build and maintain aquarium setups at SIMS. Basically, Josh turned me into a decent plumber. Josh is amazing. You're a great colleague and friend, Josh.
- **Demian Koop** and **Paula Cisternas**. Demian, thanks for the wonderful PhD advice throughout all these years. Paula, you have been a great lunch buddy -- thanks for all the advice over lunch and ramen, I have become a better person because of you two. 
- **Roberta Johnson**, **Richard Grainger** and **Dione Deaker**. These Honours students are now doing their PhDs, but back then they were my volunteers. They're the reason some people think that I can clone myself and do so many things in a day. Thanks guys! Thanks Roberta for working with me on all the crazy new ideas. We probably won't forget about those blood-gas analysers for a while. Rich, thanks for all the hard work with the feeding experiments. I would have not been able to do them without you. Dione, thank you for looking at the sea urchin spines! And for helping me throughout the end of the PhD with the random bits and pieces.
- People at the Sydney Institute of Marine Science, thank you for the opportunity to work at the aquarium facility and for accomodating my increasingly complex experimental setups. **Amanda**, **Ulysse**, **Mark** and **Peter**, SIMS is an amazing melting pot for collaboration thanks to you guys! 
- The crazy cool postgrad students at CMEG. You made the experience in the building fun. Gus and Cello, we made it! Roberta, you can do it! 

Special thanks to Kevin Keay and Frank Lovicu, who helped with various PhD matters and funding. Thanks to the Professor NGW \& Mrs Ann Macintosh Memorial Scholarship for financial support.

Last but not least, I would like to thank my wife, Cynthia, and my parents, Harianto and Lian Hiong for supporting me relentlessly throughout these years. I dedicate this thesis to my family... including our newest addition, my beautiful daughter, Freya Harianto.
